sections.What it does:
`kac` reads one corpus and judges it against the schema above it. `Program.cs` wires Spectre.Console.Cli to the verbs and runs the corpus pre-flight. Every verb's logic is in `kac.core`. Taken from the header comment in `tooling/kac/kac.csproj`.

The command surface is `new`, `validate`, `generate`, `restore`, `export`, `bundle`, `pack`, `checks`, `report` and `update`. The documentation site has a page for each verb, at <https://paul80nd.github.io/knowledge-as-code/use/cli/>.

Two walk-ups decide what it reads. `kac` walks up for `.corpus.yaml` to find the corpus, then walks up again for `.schema/` to find what to judge the corpus against. Taken from `docs/maintaining/architecture.md`.
sections.Where it lives:
* **Repository**: [`knowledge-as-code`](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code), at `tooling/kac`, with the
  engine beside it at `tooling/kac.core`
* **Platform**: .NET 10, packed as a dotnet tool
* **Deployed as**: a NuGet package on nuget.org, installed by `dotnet tool install`
sections.Dependencies:
None in this catalogue. `kac` reads a corpus from the filesystem. It calls nothing at run time.

The packages it is built from are in the tool register: [tol-spectre-console](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/cc7c513e42adfe27a4ebb551553fd67d314179bf/examples/dog-fooding/tools/build/spectre-console.md), [tol-yamldotnet](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/cc7c513e42adfe27a4ebb551553fd67d314179bf/examples/dog-fooding/tools/build/yamldotnet.md) and [tol-markdig](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/cc7c513e42adfe27a4ebb551553fd67d314179bf/examples/dog-fooding/tools/build/markdig.md). The actions that build, test and publish it are there too: [tol-checkout](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/cc7c513e42adfe27a4ebb551553fd67d314179bf/examples/dog-fooding/tools/workflows/checkout.md), [tol-setup-dotnet](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/cc7c513e42adfe27a4ebb551553fd67d314179bf/examples/dog-fooding/tools/workflows/setup-dotnet.md) and [tol-nuget-login](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/cc7c513e42adfe27a4ebb551553fd67d314179bf/examples/dog-fooding/tools/workflows/nuget-login.md).
sections.Data: None of its own. Every input is a file in the corpus it was pointed at. Every output is written back beside that corpus under `.dist/`, `.imports/` or `_reports/`. Taken from the `.gitignore` rule in [std-CONFIG](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/cc7c513e42adfe27a4ebb551553fd67d314179bf/examples/dog-fooding/standards/configuration.md).
